newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen bourse overtakes Shanghai in A shares.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen bourse overtakes Shanghai in A shares.

text.p: Volumes of China's domestic A shares surged on the Shenzhen stock exchange between April and August, surpassing turnover in Shanghai for the first time in three years, Chinese stock analysts said on Thursday.

In the five months to August from April, A share turnover in Shenzhen hit 385.9 billion yuan against 329.9 billion yuan in Shanghai. In the previous three years, Shenzhen's turnover was about 30 to 50 percent that of Shanghai's.
A shares are not open to foreign investors.
Shenzhen's A share index climbed 139.68 percent to 276.50 points at its close on Thursday from the last trading day in March while its Shanghai counterpart rose 48.18 percent over the same period.

Analysts said Shenzhen, suffering an identity crisis over its future role as a financial centre after China takes over Hong Kong in mid-1997, has made great efforts this year to raise the profile of its market and lift trading volumes.
They said A share turnover in Shenzhen was likely to remain ahead of volumes in Shanghai for the remainder of 1996.
"Since the start of this year, the Shenzhen bourse and city government have taken a series of measures to support the market," said a stock analyst with Shenyin & Wanguo Securities.

Those measures include an announcement by the city government in late April offering special support for blue-chip companies, along with a cut in trading fees by the exchange and the setting up of special stock trading promotion groups.
The analysts said Shanghai had taken similar measures but lagged behind Shenzhen this year and had failed to take the initiative or have a major impact on the market.
Officials said Shenzhen was working on more measures to boost the market for the rest of this year. Shanghai, however, appeared to have no such near-term plans, the analysts said.

"Shenzhen is likely to continue to take the lead for the rest of this year," said an analyst with China Guotai Securities. "But in the long run, Shanghai still has many advantages including support from the central government."
